card.name: Verb slot after a named subject in news
card.fires_on: The comma or helper verb (may, is, are, has) right after a subject noun phrase in news and science-feature prose, just before the main verb of the sentence. The subject is often a named person with a role, or a group such as scientists.

modes.label: Comma after subject
modes.description: A comma closing a descriptive phrase after a person's name and role, before the main verb.

modes.label: Helper verb after subject
modes.description: A helper verb such as may, is, are or has right after the subject, before the main verb.
modes.example: Now, nootkatone<< may>> find another use: repelling blackleg

card.writes: It pushes toward words like keeping and away from odd, unrelated tokens, but the effect is weak and unclear.
card.plain: It fires at the point in a news sentence where the subject has just been named and the main verb is about to come.
